jurisdiction: School Board of Orange County, Florida (Orange County Public Schools). Every Orange County voter, including all of Orlando, sees this question.
number: School Board Question: The School Board of Orange County, Florida Ad Valorem Millage Election
official_title: Shall the School Board of Orange County, Florida, continue the current one mill ad valorem millage for essential operating expenses, including compensating teachers and educational support employees, preserving academic programs, arts, athletics, and student activities, beginning July 1, 2027, and ending four fiscal years later on June 30, 2031, shared proportionately with charter schools as legally required, with annual reporting to ensure proper fiscal stewardship of these funds to the citizens of Orange County?
plain_summary: Renews an extra school property tax Orange County already pays: 1 mill, or $1 per $1,000 of taxable value, for four more years (July 2027 to June 2031). The district says it raises about $255 million a year, mostly for teacher and staff pay.
yes_means: The extra 1-mill school tax continues from July 2027 through June 2031, at the same rate you pay now.
no_means: The extra 1-mill school tax ends on June 30, 2027, and the district loses what it says is about $255 million a year.
current_law: Voters have approved this extra 1 mill every time it has been on the ballot since 2010. The current approval runs through June 30, 2027, so nothing changes before then whichever way this vote goes.
fiscal_impact: District figures as reported by WKMG News 6 (Aug 24, 2026): about $255 million a year, funding about 2,000 teaching positions. For a home appraised at $355,000, the district says the tax costs about $28 a month. A school board member told The Apopka Chief that roughly 90% of the money goes to teacher and support-staff pay. No official ballot explanation or independent fiscal note was found.
confusing_wording_note: Three things trip people up. (1) The choices are printed 'Yes for Approval' and 'No for Rejection.' Yes keeps the tax; No ends it. (2) 'Continue' means this renews a tax you already pay; it isn't a new or higher tax. (3) It doesn't start until July 1, 2027, because the current approval covers the next school year. Also, Amendment 3's bigger homestead break is only for non-school taxes, so it wouldn't change this school tax.

supporters_case.text: The school district and board say the levy pays for about 2,000 positions and supports raises; OCPS's spokesperson said 'This is not costing the taxpayers any more money. It's a continuation of what we currently have.' Board Chair Teresa Jacobs said 'the cost of educating students is rising faster than the revenue available to support them,' citing employee health-care costs.

opponents_case.text: No organized campaign against the renewal turned up in our sources. The closest criticism: School Board District 3 candidate Diana Moore wrote that the levy 'was sold to the public to attract and retain quality teachers' but has no citizen oversight committee, and that a proposal to earmark part of it for teacher raises failed on the board. She did not say how she will vote on it.
